candidates.claim: The first entry of CORP_IN (fw-01:60), bound inbound on the corp interface (fw-01:103), permits 192.168.30.102 to open tcp/502 to 10.10.10.21 in OT, which is matched before the CORP-to-OT deny at pos 3.
candidates.remediation: Remove the permit at fw-01:60 from CORP_IN and block CORP access to OT, since no CORP-to-OT service is approved.

candidates.claim: The effective permit at fw-01:60 allows CORP-to-OT tcp/502 traffic that is not among the approved cross-zone services A1-A7, bypassing DMZ mediation.
candidates.remediation: Remove the permit at fw-01:60 so that all CORP-to-OT traffic is denied, as the approved services require.

candidates.claim: The line access-list CORP_IN permit tcp 192.168.30.102 to 10.10.10.21 eq 502 is present in the current snapshot at fw-01:60 but is absent from the approved baseline.
candidates.remediation: Reconcile this deviation by removing the entry at fw-01:60 or, if it is authorized, documenting its approval and updating the baseline.

clarifications.question: The switch port roles say only OT-facing ports may be active in VLAN 10, but the approved trunks carry VLAN 10 on non-OT-facing ports: sw-core-01 Gi1/0/22 {10,99} and sw-core-01 Gi1/0/24 {10,20,30,99}, plus the OT uplink sw-ot-01 Gi1/0/24 {10,99}. Are these approved trunks an exception to the VLAN 10 rule, or should VLAN 10 be carried only on OT-facing ports?
